lessonIndex.title: A.1 Kinematics
lessonIndex.summary: Kinematics provides the mathematical tools needed to describe motion. By understanding displacement, velocity, acceleration and motion graphs, students are able to analyse and predict the movement of objects. These concepts form the foundation for mechanics and are essential for further topics in IB Physics.
learning_objectives: Understand the difference between scalar and vector quantities.
Explain the difference between speed and velocity.
Calculate acceleration using changes in velocity.
Apply equations of motion for objects with constant acceleration.

lessonIndex.title: A.2 Forces and Momentum
lessonIndex.summary: Forces and momentum explain how objects interact and change their motion. Newton's laws provide the foundation for analysing forces, while momentum conservation allows prediction of outcomes in collisions and explosions. These principles are essential in mechanics and many engineering applications.

lessonIndex.title: A.3 Work, Energy and Power
lessonIndex.summary: Work, energy and power provide a method to analyse how energy moves and changes in physical systems. By applying conservation of energy, students can understand mechanical systems, calculate energy transfers and evaluate efficiency. These concepts are used throughout physics, engineering and technology.
learning_objectives: Explain energy transfer and energy transformation.
Calculate work done by a force.

lessonIndex.title: A.4 Rigid Body Mechanics
lessonIndex.summary: Rigid body mechanics explains how objects rotate, balance and respond to turning forces. Understanding torque, moments, centre of mass and angular momentum allows physicists and engineers to analyse complex systems from machines to spacecraft.

lessonIndex.title: A.5 Relativity
lessonIndex.summary: Relativity changes the way physicists understand space, time and energy. Special relativity explains how measurements depend on motion, while the mass-energy relationship shows the connection between matter and energy. These concepts are essential for modern physics, astronomy, particle physics and advanced technology.
learning_objectives: Understand the need for relativity in physics.
Understand the postulates of special relativity.
Explain time dilation and length contraction.
Understand relativistic effects at high speeds.

lessonIndex.title: B.1 Thermal Physics
lessonIndex.summary: Thermal physics explains how particles behave and how energy transfers between systems. Understanding temperature, internal energy, heat transfer and gas laws allows physicists to analyse materials, machines and natural processes. These concepts are essential for thermodynamics and many real-world technologies.
learning_objectives: Understand the particle model of matter.

lessonIndex.title: B.2 Greenhouse Effect
lessonIndex.summary: The greenhouse effect explains how Earth's atmosphere maintains temperature through infrared absorption and re-emission. The natural greenhouse effect supports life, while increased greenhouse gas concentrations strengthen warming. Understanding radiation, energy balance and climate feedback helps explain modern climate changes.
learning_objectives: Explain how electromagnetic radiation interacts with the atmosphere.
Identify greenhouse gases and their roles.
Analyse energy balance in Earth's climate system.

lessonIndex.title: B.3 Gas Laws
lessonIndex.summary: Gas laws explain how pressure, volume and temperature are connected through the motion of particles. By understanding kinetic theory and applying gas equations, physicists can predict gas behaviour in natural systems, machines and technology.
learning_objectives: Understand the behaviour of gas particles.

lessonIndex.title: B.4 Thermodynamics
lessonIndex.summary: Thermodynamics explains how energy transfers occur in physical systems. The first law describes energy conservation, while the second law explains the direction of energy transfer and the increase of entropy. These principles are essential for understanding engines, refrigerators, power generation and natural processes.
learning_objectives: Apply the first law of thermodynamics.
Understand heat transfer and work done.
Explain entropy and the second law of thermodynamics.

lessonIndex.title: C.1 Simple Harmonic Motion
lessonIndex.summary: Simple harmonic motion describes repeated oscillations where the restoring force is proportional to displacement. Understanding SHM helps explain vibrations, waves, engineering systems and natural phenomena. Concepts such as damping, resonance, energy transfer and oscillation equations are essential for analysing periodic motion.
learning_objectives: Explain equilibrium position and restoring force.
Analyse displacement, velocity and acceleration relationships.

lessonIndex.title: C.2 Wave Properties
lessonIndex.summary: Wave properties explain how waves transfer energy and interact with their surroundings. Understanding reflection, refraction, diffraction, interference, standing waves and the Doppler effect allows analysis of sound, light and modern communication technologies.
learning_objectives: Differentiate between transverse and longitudinal waves.
Define wavelength, frequency, amplitude and wave speed.

lessonIndex.title: C.3 Wave Phenomena
lessonIndex.summary: Wave phenomena explain how waves interact with materials and with each other. Reflection, refraction, diffraction, interference and polarisation are used in many technologies including communication, medicine and engineering. Understanding these behaviours allows prediction and analysis of wave systems.
learning_objectives: Explain reflection and refraction of waves.
Understand wave behaviour in different media.
Apply wave phenomena to real applications.

lessonIndex.title: C.4 Fields
lessonIndex.summary: Fields explain how objects interact without direct contact. Gravitational, electric and magnetic fields are used to describe forces, energy transfer and motion. These concepts are important for understanding satellites, electricity generation, motors and modern technology.

lessonIndex.title: C.5 Electromagnetic Induction
lessonIndex.summary: Electromagnetic induction explains how changing magnetic fields create electrical energy. Faraday's law describes the magnitude of induced emf, while Lenz's law explains its direction. These principles form the basis of generators, transformers, motors and many modern electrical technologies.

lessonIndex.title: D.1 Electric Fields
lessonIndex.summary: Electric fields explain how charged objects interact without contact. Coulomb's law, electric field strength, potential, capacitors and particle acceleration are important concepts used in physics and technology. Understanding electric fields helps explain circuits, electronics and advanced scientific equipment.
learning_objectives: Understand electric fields and electric field strength.
Understand electric potential and potential energy.

lessonIndex.title: D.2 Magnetic Fields
lessonIndex.summary: Magnetic fields explain how magnets and moving charges interact. Magnetic forces produce motion in motors, control particles in accelerators and enable technologies such as MRI and mass spectrometry. Understanding magnetic fields is essential for electromagnetism and modern physics.
learning_objectives: Understand forces on current carrying conductors.

lessonIndex.title: D.3 Electromagnetic Waves
lessonIndex.summary: Electromagnetic waves transfer energy through oscillating electric and magnetic fields. The electromagnetic spectrum contains waves with different wavelengths, frequencies and energies. Their properties allow applications in communication, medicine, astronomy and technology while requiring safety controls for high energy radiation.
learning_objectives: Understand wave properties of electromagnetic radiation.
Analyse risks and benefits of electromagnetic radiation.

lessonIndex.title: D.4 Quantum Physics
lessonIndex.summary: Quantum physics explains the behaviour of matter and radiation at atomic scales. Concepts such as photons, energy quantisation, the photoelectric effect and wave-particle duality explain modern technologies including lasers, electronics and medical equipment.
learning_objectives: Understand the quantum nature of light.

lessonIndex.title: D.5 Nuclear Physics
lessonIndex.summary: Nuclear physics explains the structure and behaviour of atomic nuclei. Radioactive decay, fission and fusion describe how nuclei change and release energy. These principles are used in power generation, medicine, research and space technology.
